name: Sea-level rise (IPCC AR6)
summary: Applies published IPCC AR6 relative sea-level projections to coastal point data. Consumes projections; does not produce them.

hostCapabilities.note: Satisfied by the host's table_input widget 0.1.0 (urn:fieldwork:widget:table_input), which imports a long-format CSV keyed by declared columns and emits fw:DataTable with a stated or unstated unit, and by table_output 0.4.0 in its table mode. The host's key tuple must be unique, which an extract keyed by site, scenario, workflow, family, year and quantile satisfies. Present in fieldwork main as unreleased work; a released host version is not yet claimed. See fieldwork docs/experiments/48-tabular-input.md. The three widget contracts this pack declared are now implemented in the host, so the pack no longer declares widgets of its own.

keyFields.note: An extract that will be joined to Philippine administrative boundaries must key on the official PSGC code, not a place name: names repeat across provinces and a name-keyed join matches the wrong polygon without failing. The boundary vintage the codes came from is recorded in provenance, because PSGC codes are renumbered when units are reclassified.

boundarySources.note: Excluded as a pack dependency: a pack publishes its data, which its licence forbids. Usable only for a practitioner’s own local exploration.

kinds.workflow: the value came from one published workflow, such as wf_1e
kinds.confidence-pbox: the value was read from a confidence output file, which is a p-box combining workflow p-boxes

basis.note: Measured 2026-10-09 from total_ssp245_medium_confidence_values.nc: the confidence output files carry no workflow dimension, and their source attribute names the workflow p-boxes they combine. A key component assuming one workflow could not describe them, so the identifier and the kind of identifier are declared separately. A p-box bound is not a quantile of one distribution and the two kinds are not interchangeable.

discovery.note: Out of scope by decision: the practitioner has already obtained the dataset. Which workflow, scenario and dataset family they chose is recorded on import, not chosen here.

acquisition.note: Out of scope by decision, not by impossibility. This previously read "Impossible in a browser for this data", which was measured to be wrong on 2026-10-10: Zenodo serves this record with access-control-allow-origin: * and honours Range requests, answering 206 with a Content-Range, and the summary file for one scenario and family is 71.7 MB deflated inside the 9.24 GB archive. A browser can read the zip central directory from a tail range and fetch that member alone. The size argument was also unsound in its own terms: a store's size is not the bytes a reader transfers, as reading 55,649 of 81,455,423 rows from 11 GB of Overture GeoParquet demonstrates. The Monte Carlo sample stores really are 38.42 GB and 1.65 TB, and their cross-origin reachability has not been measured. What stands is the decision: extraction needs dataset-specific knowledge — which variable, which dimension order, which quantile index — and that belongs where a reader can see and re-run it, not inside a widget. The pinned Pyodide kernel in the validation lab carries netcdf4 and zarr, so the extraction is reproducible there without installing anything.

extraction.note: scripts/extract-projection.py selects the sites, scenarios, years and quantiles a workflow needs and writes a long-format CSV with a provenance record. Run outside the application by decision: choosing the selection needs dataset-specific knowledge — which variable, which dimension order, which quantile index — and that belongs where a reader can see and re-run it. Not because a browser cannot read the data; it can, and stages.acquisition records the measurement. The validation lab's pinned Pyodide kernel carries netcdf4, xarray and zarr.

import.note: The host's Tabular data widget reads the long-format CSV and slr_extract_import declares it as a bounded extract. The pack's own import contract is superseded.

application.note: The host implements these three contracts natively as urn:fieldwork:widget:slr_extract_import, slr_site_assignment and slr_threshold_comparison, because the application loads no pack and this pack ships no code. This pack remains the source of the vocabulary, the shapes and the worked example; the host vendors the two TTL files at the digests the curated catalog pins. See fieldwork docs/experiments/58-sea-level-widgets.md.

measured.note: Read for the first time on this date. Values are millimetres, not metres. No attribute carries the baseline period; it is stated from AR6 WG1 Chapter 9 documentation. The file declares no Conventions, so CF semantics cannot be assumed.

dataSources.name: IPCC AR6 projection site list
dataSources.note: 228 Philippine rows redistributed as examples/manila-coastal-exposure/projection-sites-ph.csv; the published list has 66,190 rows.

supersededWidgets.note: These contracts were declared here and are implemented in the host. They are listed for history: a pack that cannot ship code is a specification, and the thing that can execute it implements it. Deviations from the declared contracts are argued in fieldwork docs/experiments/58-sea-level-widgets.md.

widgets.deviation: Takes a table input rather than importing the CSV itself: the host already has a tabular importer, and a second reader of the same file would be a second place for the contract to drift.

Three inputs rather than two. A table has no geometry in the host (fw:DataTable is disjoint from fw:PointDataset), so the published sites arrive as a point layer rather than inside the projections table. The output is a table of distances, so the join can be displayed.
None of substance. Refuses a missing datum, a missing elevation attribute and a partial key, as declared, and outputs the host decisions port so it cannot reach a raster output.
